resources.string: No checks yet. Choose a photo or video to get started.
How to check a Reel, photo or video
Open the photo, video or Reel in Instagram, WhatsApp, your gallery or any other app.
Read the result. Nothing leaves your phone.
You can also pick a photo or video from your phone on the home screen.
The checks point to AI. It\'s still an estimate: real photos are sometimes flagged.
Genned can\'t tell. Treat it as no answer. Scores from about %1$d%% to %2$d%% land here, because in that range the detector is wrong too often.
No sign of AI was found. That isn\'t proof it\'s real: new AI tools, edits and screenshots can hide the signs.
Some files carry a signed record of how they were made. When Genned can verify that record, it decides the result, with no guessing.
Share the original file when you can. Screenshots and re-uploads lose detail and the signed record.
Videos can be up to 3 minutes long. Genned looks at a few frames, not the sound or the motion.
Every check runs on your phone. Genned has no internet access.
The checks point to AI. This is an estimate, not proof.
The checks aren\'t confident either way. Treat this as no answer.
This score is high, but Genned only says \"likely AI-generated\" at %1$d%% or more. Below that it is wrong too often. Treat this as no answer.
This score is low, but Genned only says \"likely not AI-generated\" below %1$d%%. Above that it is wrong too often. Treat this as no answer.
No sign of AI was found. That isn\'t proof it\'s real: new AI tools and edited pictures can slip through.
This comes from a signed record inside the file, checked on your phone. It shows what the signer declared, and nothing more.
It will be removed from your history on this phone.
This is an estimate, not proof. AI-content detection can produce false positives and false negatives.
Genned couldn\'t open this file as a picture. JPEG, PNG and WEBP work on every phone; other formats depend on your Android version.
This picture file is damaged or can\'t be read.
This picture is too large to check on this phone.

Something went wrong while checking this video. Please try again.
Genned couldn\'t read this video. It may be damaged or in a format this phone can\'t play.
Videos longer than 3 minutes can\'t be checked. Trim it or share a shorter clip.
This check is no longer available
It may have been deleted from your history.
AI tool\'s name in the file
This deletes every saved check on this device. This can\'t be undone.
Your images and videos are analyzed only on this device. Genned has no internet permission, so it can\'t upload anything: no images, results or usage data.
On-device visual classifier: not bundled in this build. Metadata-based checks still run.
Genned is built on these open-source libraries and bundles these open-source detector models. Tap an entry for its full license text.
A floating bubble for checking Reels and posts without leaving Instagram or WhatsApp. It looks at your screen only when you tap it.
Check Reels without leaving Instagram or WhatsApp
Turn on a floating bubble and tap it on any post.
A small bubble floats over Instagram and WhatsApp. Tap it to check the post or Reel on screen. Genned looks at your screen only at the moment you tap, and nothing leaves your phone.
Allow the bubble to show over other apps
Android opens its settings. Switch Genned on, then come back.
Let Genned know when Instagram or WhatsApp is open
Called \"usage access\". Genned only learns which app is in front, never what is in it.
Android asks this every time you turn the bubble on. Choose to share the entire screen.
Open Instagram or WhatsApp and tap the bubble on a post. Tap the result to see the details. Drag the bubble to the ✕ at the bottom of the screen to turn it off.
It keeps your last result and has a Stop button. Without it the bubble still works.
Genned bubble turned off. Turn it on again in Genned.
Genned couldn\'t check the screen. Tap to try again.
Tap the floating bubble over Instagram or WhatsApp to check what\'s on screen.
Genned overlay stopped: screen capture permission ended. Turn the overlay back on in Settings to keep using it.

If the overlay bubble isn\'t behaving right (not appearing over an app, or using more battery than expected), copy the log below and share it — it only contains app package names, timestamps, and the bubble\'s show/hide decisions, never any screen content.

resources.string: The file has no camera details (make, model, exposure). That\'s normal for AI pictures, and also for real photos that were screenshotted or sent through a messaging or social app, so it says little.
No AI tool left its name in the file. That doesn\'t mean the picture is real: social and messaging apps usually remove this information.
The file contains a \"parameters\" note, where Stable Diffusion tools save their generation settings.
The file\'s details (%1$s) name an AI image tool.
The file\'s details (%1$s) contain AI generation settings.
Genned can\'t check for hidden AI watermarks (such as SynthID) on the phone yet.
No Content Credentials (C2PA) in this file. Most apps and social networks remove them, so this says nothing either way.
Verified Content Credentials signed by %1$s say this was made or edited with generative AI.
Verified Content Credentials signed by %1$s say this was captured with a camera, with no generative AI declared.
Verified Content Credentials signed by %1$s were found, but they don\'t say whether generative AI was used.
Content Credentials in this file say generative AI was used, but the signer (%1$s) is not on the trusted list, so this was not counted as proof.
Content Credentials signed by %1$s were found, but the signer is not on the trusted list, so they were not used.
Content Credentials were found but failed verification (the file may have been changed after signing), so they were not used.
This file links to Content Credentials stored online. Genned never goes online, so they were not checked.
Content Credentials can\'t be checked for this file type.
Checking Content Credentials needs Android 9 or newer.
Checking Content Credentials isn\'t available on this device\'s processor type.
Content Credentials could not be read from this file.
Checking Content Credentials took too long and was skipped.
AI detection is an estimate. It can flag real pictures and miss AI ones, especially from the newest AI tools.
The AI detector didn\'t run on this one, so the estimate above rests on file details only and is less reliable.
No verified signed record (Content Credentials) was found, so there\'s no proof of where this came from.
No AI tool\'s name was found in the file. That doesn\'t mean it\'s real: social and editing apps usually remove it.
AI tool\'s name in the file
